note.explanation: Mechanical and electronic balances measure mass. A force meter measures force directly in newtons. An electronic balance needs a power supply or, in some models, dry-cell batteries; it does not need standard weights.
examples: A mechanical balance compares an object with standard weights.
A force meter can show the weight of an object in newtons.
note.checkAnswer: A force meter measures force directly in newtons (N).
note.simple: Balances measure mass; a force meter measures force.
note.checkQuestion: Which instrument measures force directly in newtons?
note.title: Balances and force meters
steps: Use a mechanical balance with standard weights to compare masses.
Use a mechanical platform balance for heavy items; its calibrated small weights are used instead of separate standard weights.
Connect an electronic balance to a power supply, or use a model that operates on dry-cell batteries.
Use a force meter to measure force in newtons; if a spring balance scale shows mass in kilograms, multiply by g = 10 m s⁻² to find the weight in newtons.
note.answer: A force meter, also called a newton meter or spring balance, measures force directly in newtons (N).

examTips: This section is most likely to be tested through short-answer questions about the construction, use, or purpose of each instrument.
For a comparison question, state clearly that balances measure mass while a force meter measures force in newtons.
For a force-meter question, earn marks by describing the spring, hook, pointer, and zero reading when the hook is empty.
For a platform-balance question, mention that its fulcrum is near one end and its smaller weights are calibrated to standard weights.

Put standard weights in the other pan.

explain.title: Mechanical balances
explain.body: A mechanical balance consists of a rigid horizontal beam that oscillates on a central knife edge as a fulcrum. It has two end knife edges equidistant from the centre. Two pans are hung from bearings on the end knife edges. Put the object in one pan and standard weights in the other, then adjust the weights until the beam is in equilibrium.

explain.title: Platform balances
explain.body: A mechanical platform balance is used for heavy items such as flour bags, cement bags, and steel bars. Its fulcrum is very near one end of the beam, so smaller weights can balance the load. These smaller weights have already been calibrated to standard weights.

explain.title: Electronic balances
explain.body: An electronic balance does not need standard weights. It must be connected to a power supply, although some models use dry-cell batteries. It displays the mass, and some models can display the total price if the rate per kg is entered.

explain.title: Force meters
explain.body: A force meter is a scientific instrument that measures force. It is also called as a newton meter or a spring balance. It measures force directly in newtons (N), unlike balances, which measure mass in kilograms or its multiples.

explain.title: How an ordinary force meter works
explain.body: An ordinary force meter has a spring, a handle, a hook, a pointer, and a scale in newtons. The pointer coincides with zero when nothing is hung from the hook. Hanging an object makes the spring compress or stretch, and the pointer indicates the object's weight.

mistakes: Do not say that a balance measures force in newtons; balances measure mass.
Do not confuse mass in kilograms with weight in newtons.
Do not forget that an ordinary force meter should read zero when nothing is hung from its hook.
Do not say that all electronic balances must use dry-cell batteries; some models use them, while the balance must be connected to a power supply.
Do not claim that a mechanical platform balance uses no calibrated weights; its smaller weights are calibrated to standard weights.
